artists.biography: Stiff Little Fingers are a punk rock band from Belfast, Northern Ireland. They formed in 1977, at the height of the Troubles. They started out as a schoolboy band called Highway Star (named after the Deep Purple song), doing rock covers, until they discovered punk. They split up after six years and four albums, although they reformed five years later, in 1987. Despite major personnel changes, they are still touring and recording as of 2011. Jake Burns, their lead singer, is the only member to have been with the band during all its incarnations, but in March 2006, original bass guitarist Ali McMordie rejoined them following the departure of The Jam bass player Bruce Foxton after fifteen years.

The album serves as a retrospective of the band's work during their initial period of activity, drawing from their most significant recordings across their first several studio albums. As a greatest hits collection, it represents a consolidation of the group's punk and post-punk output during the late 1970s and early 1980s, a period that established them as key figures in the UK punk movement.

The compilation captures Stiff Little Fingers' evolution from their raw, politically charged early punk sound toward the more refined rock approach they developed across successive releases. The album's track selection highlights the band's signature blend of aggressive instrumentation, socially conscious lyrics, and the distinctive Northern Irish perspective that informed much of their work. By 1983, the band had already established a substantial catalog of singles and album tracks that demonstrated their range within the punk and rock idiom.

The release of "All the Best" in 1983 positioned the band's catalog for broader accessibility during a period when compilation albums served as important entry points for new listeners. The album reflects Stiff Little Fingers' commercial and critical standing at that point in their career, documenting a band that had maintained relevance and artistic credibility through the transition from punk's initial explosion to its various post-punk and alternative rock offshoots.
